result.summary: This residential intersection lacks basic pedestrian crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control signs. While sidewalks are present on both sides of the street, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the corners create visibility and accessibility challenges for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection to designate pedestrian right-of-way.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles close to the intersection corners block the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbsides near the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of sloped curb transitions makes the crossing inaccessible for people with mobility aids or strollers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection characterized by row housing and a complete absence of pedestrian crossing infrastructure. There are no marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or visible traffic control devices, and parked vehicles near the corners create potential sightline obstructions. The environment prioritizes vehicle movement and storage over pedestrian safety and accessibility.
